title: Choose the public site composition
question: Bolder hand. Earlier masthead, scroll, ledger, timetable, daylight, and VU are out. The roll assigned Capability switchboard. Sticker-album slots were dropped: empty outlines would advertise unpublished drafts.

options.label: Capability switchboard
options.thesis: The public page names the installed packages first: Site and Journal, then renders the one you are reading.
options.viewport: Horizontal ink switch of Site and Journal; paper below shows the landing statement with the first published notes already in view.
options.risk: Can read as an app shell if the switch steals the statement’s job.

raised.raise: Landing and notes share one column grid; captions live inside it, not as a separate chrome family.
A published count is a visible decimal event in the strip, not a badge decoration.

options.label: Facing formes
options.thesis: Two printer’s plates on one sheet: landing on the left, notes on the right, bound by a spine rule.
options.viewport: Split sheet: statement occupies the left forme; dated notes occupy the right; both visible without a tab.
options.risk: Narrow screens must stack plates without turning into a generic two-column blog.

options.label: Applied tray
options.thesis: Only applied work is in public: the landing is the tray label, published notes sit as printed slips.
materials: amber never appears on this surface
options.viewport: Tray heading from the landing record, then a stack of published slips with title, date, and excerpt already showing.
options.risk: Can feel like a review queue if slips look like pending cards.

options.label: Build instructions
options.thesis: The public site is the assembled model: Site is step one, each published note is a later piece seated on the studs.
options.viewport: Oversized step numeral, landing as the seated base, latest note marked as the piece that just clicked down.
options.case: This example is an assembled product; numbered seating makes builder versus work legible without a marketing hero.
options.risk: Sky-blue toy grammar would fight Kernel; steps must stay ink, paper, and square.

options.label: Curved crease
options.thesis: One structural rule lifts the landing; published notes remain the flat remainder of the same sheet.
options.viewport: A single ink arc-as-rule across paper; landing sits above it at larger scale; notes occupy the planar field below.
options.case: One line produces the hierarchy, so the page stays one object instead of hero-plus-feed.
options.risk: A literal curve or cream stock would abandon Kernel’s square cool paper.

options.label: ASCII live scene
options.thesis: The journal as a strict character grid whose density stands in for hierarchy.
options.viewport: A fixed grid where landing and notes are cells of the same alphabet.
options.case: Fuses poorly: visitors came to read a workspace journal, not a glyph sculpture.
options.kept: One shared column grid; no second chrome family for the notes.
options.risk: Phosphor-on-black would invent a terminal identity Kernel does not own.
